subject: physics
question_text: What happens to the time period of a simple pendulum when the lift carrying it moves up with an acceleration a?

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The effective g
lines: In a lift going up with acceleration a, the
floor pushes up harder on the bob, and the
effective value of g acting on it becomes
steps.why: Only g changes; the length of the string and the mass of the bob do not, so every lift question is one substitution.
common_mistakes: Changing the length or the mass instead of g.

recall.must_convey: That the effective g becomes g plus a when the lift accelerates upward.

steps.label: The time period
lines: T is SMALLER than on the ground, so the
pendulum swings faster. If the lift goes down
with acceleration a the effective value is
g − a, and T is larger.
steps.why: In free fall a = g, the effective value is zero and T becomes infinite — the same answer as a pendulum in a satellite.
common_mistakes: Using g + a for a lift moving down as well; the sign follows the direction of the acceleration, not the motion.

recall.must_convey: That T is 2 pi root l by g plus a, smaller than on the ground.
accept: 2 pi root l by g plus a
reject: g plus a is the effective value
